clue.text: Cube, for example, by past master?

parts.note: past means over, as in 'the danger is past'
a cube is the third power of a number, so it is an example of a power

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a geometric cube was made by some old master craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cube' looks like a solid shape, but here it is the mathematical sense, raising a number to the third power.
explanation.definitionFit: To master someone is to defeat or subdue them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Curses as horse tucked into food

indicators.note: the horse letter is tucked inside the word for food

parts.note: oats are food, especially for horses
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A rider swears as the horse tucks into its feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' puts H inside OATS. 'Horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths are swear words, a synonym for curses.

clue.text: Simple addition in road movie

parts.note: easy means simple
a rider is a clause added to a document

explanation.surface: An easy extra scene added to a film about the open road.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy Rider is the 1969 road movie starring Dennis Hopper and Peter Fonda.

clue.text: Outwardly devout, nameless friend turned treacherous

indicators.note: the devout word stands on the outside, around the other piece

parts.note: pious means devout

indicators.note: turned means rearranged, so the letters change order
nameless means lacking a name, and N is the usual abbreviation for name, so that letter is dropped from the friend

explanation.surface: A friend who appeared devout on the outside turned out to be a traitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' makes the devout word a shell around the rest; the surface reads it as a hypocrite's outward show of piety.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfidious means faithless and deceitful, a synonym of treacherous.

clue.text: Females in novel about game (abridged)

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: novel means new

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: chess is a game

explanation.surface: Women characters in a book about some game, in a shortened edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NEW into WEN; 'abridged' cuts CHESS to CHES.
explanation.definitionFit: Wenches is an old word for young women, so it means females.

clue.text: Action demanded after ballot, say?

definitions.meaning: a second count of votes when an election result is close
to ... a story is to narrate or tell it

explanation.definitionFit: A recount counts votes again; to recount is also to relate a story.

clue.text: Confronted with coffee from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading from right to left, so the word is turned around

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Someone was handed a cup of coffee brought from eastern lands.
explanation.definitionFit: Faced and confronted are synonyms: to face a problem is to confront it.

clue.text: Very affectionate, but discovered to be non-U

indicators.note: non-U means without U, the letter is taken away

parts.note: found means discovered

explanation.surface: Someone loving is found to be not upper class.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper class; here it means without the letter U.
explanation.definitionFit: Fond means having affection, close in meaning to very affectionate.

clue.text: Band of brothers initially plunged in lake

indicators.note: the first letter plunges into the lake word

parts.note: Lake Como is in northern Italy

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter

explanation.surface: A group of brothers dive into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes B from 'brothers'; 'plunged in' puts it in COMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A combo is a small jazz or dance band.

clue.text: One seems gutted, gloomy about being fired

indicators.note: the gloomy word goes about the others, enclosing them

parts.note: dismal means gloomy
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: gutted removes the inside, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone seems devastated and gloomy about losing their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like an emotion to go with 'gloomy', but it means emptied out, leaving only the end letters of 'seems'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismissal is being sacked from a job, the same as being fired.

clue.text: Stunner tried again to pass round

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a student who resat an exam took it again hoping to pass

explanation.surface: A student repeated an exam hoping to get through it, and the result was a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns RESAT around to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electroshock weapon that stuns its target, so it is literally a stunner.

clue.text: Scarface and Bugsy, for example, perpetrate identity theft

definitions.meaning: Scarface (Al Capone) and Bugsy (Siegel) are gangsters' informal monikers
to nick is British slang for steal, so to steal names is identity theft

explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface and Bugsy are informal labels for gangsters; read as two words it means steal monikers.

clue.text: Truly sounding like one of Bo-Peep's flock?

indicators.note: sounding like says the words are spoken and the result is what we hear

parts.note: Little Bo-Peep lost her sheep in the nursery rhyme, so one of them is a strayed tup, a tup being a ram

explanation.surface: A whimsical claim that being honest is like one of the nursery-rhyme shepherdess's sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Bo-Peep is a nursery rhyme in which the shepherdess loses her sheep; TUP is a British word for a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is an informal phrase meaning honestly or truly.

clue.text: Try swinging both ways in desert

parts.note: to have a go is to try
slang for bisexual, shortened to bi

explanation.surface: Someone experiments with both directions while lost in the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a large desert in Mongolia and northern China, an example of a desert.

clue.text: Disagreement with complaint following military command

indicators.note: following places the complaint after the command

parts.note: fall in is a drill order to line up
gout is a painful illness, a complaint

explanation.surface: A soldier grumbles about an order, causing a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a quarrel or disagreement.

clue.text: Birds move round one on seafront

indicators.note: the word for move goes round the one, enclosing it

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
I is the Roman numeral one
the front of the word sea is S

explanation.surface: Birds on the promenade shuffle around someone standing there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts BUDGE around I to give BUDGIE, and S, the front letter of 'sea', ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Budgies, short for budgerigars, are small parrots, an example of birds.

clue.text: Unsustainable activity? Dupe's about to have something to chew on

parts.note: an economic bubble is a boom that cannot last

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a mug is a fool or dupe

explanation.surface: Someone fooled is given something to think about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MUG into GUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubblegum is chewing gum that can be blown into bubbles.

clue.text: A great side's debut, playing a blinder

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are moved around in play, signalling a rearrangement
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter of side's is taken

explanation.surface: A football team's first match is a brilliant performance, a blinder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges AGREAT into TEARGA; 'debut' takes S from 'side's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tear gas blinds people temporarily with stinging, so it is cryptically something that blinds.

clue.text: Innocent officer implicated in deceit on ship

indicators.note: the officer is implicated, placed inside the word for deceit

parts.note: guile means cunning deceit
LT is short for lieutenant
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An officer is falsely accused of trickery aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Guiltless means free of guilt, innocent.

clue.text: Ships that are worse than their bights?

definitions.text: Ships that are worse than their bights?

parts.words: Ships that are worse than their bights?
parts.note: plays on the saying that someone's bark is worse than their bite, with sailing vessels sounding like barks and bays (bights) sounding like bites

explanation.definitionFit: Barques are three-masted sailing ships, matching ships in the clue.

clue.text: Training or diets that may boost performance?

indicators.note: training suggests the letters are put through exercises, rearranged

explanation.surface: Athletes ask whether training or diets will improve performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' rearranges ORDIETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Anabolic steroids are drugs athletes use to boost performance.

clue.text: College graduate sick about having nothing left

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for sick is read backwards

parts.note: ill means sick
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A college graduate feels ill after being left with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns ILL into LLI. Balliol is one of the colleges of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Balliol is an Oxford college, an example of a college.

clue.text: Big emu left United Kingdom?

indicators.note: united means put together, here the letters are joined in a new order

explanation.surface: A large flightless bird has departed from Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' rearranges BIGEMU and L. 'United Kingdom' looks like Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgium is a constitutional monarchy, so it is a kingdom.

clue.text: Fish not caught, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the clue word sounds like the answer

parts.note: an animal not caught is loose, free

explanation.surface: An angler complains that the fish got away.
explanation.definitionFit: Luce is an old name for the pike, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Young guns?

parts.note: read as young horses that share a name with a brand of revolver

explanation.definitionFit: Colts are young male horses, and Colt revolvers are guns.

clue.text: Something afoot in the capital

parts.note: read literally, something on one's foot, a boot, which shares its name with New Zealand's capital city

explanation.walkthrough: A wellington is a rubber boot in British English; Wellington is also the capital of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A wellington boot is worn on the foot, and the city is New Zealand's capital.

clue.text: Resort to an auditor who's one of the family?

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is heard

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: An accountant goes on holiday to a seaside resort with a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member.

clue.text: Someone famous for the biggest part?

definitions.text: Someone famous for the biggest part?

parts.words: Someone famous for the biggest part?
parts.note: refers to the phrase about taking the largest share, named after a big cat; also a celebrity

explanation.definitionFit: A lion is a celebrity, and the lion's share is the biggest part.

clue.text: Campaign in which a soldier guards the whole churchgoing force?

indicators.note: the soldier guards the other piece by standing on either side of it

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
all means the whole

indicators.note: split as church going: CE (Church of England) goes from the word

parts.note: the police force

explanation.surface: A military campaign in which one soldier protects a whole force of devout troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'churchgoing' reads as devout, but splits as church (CE, Church of England) plus going, so CE leaves the word for force. Gallipoli was fought in 1915-16.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallipoli was the First World War campaign in Turkey of 1915-16.

clue.text: Award someone extremely corpulent

parts.note: the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the outer letters of someone

explanation.surface: A very fat person is given an honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes S and E from 'someone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese and corpulent are synonyms for very overweight.

clue.text: Dixon's partner may be found in lodge

definitions.meaning: Charles ... surveyed the ...-Dixon line with Jeremiah Dixon

explanation.definitionFit: Mason partnered Dixon on the famous boundary survey; a Freemason belongs to a lodge.

clue.text: Cup of coffee or tea missed out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of order, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone missed their tea and had to choose a coffee instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEAMISSED.
explanation.definitionFit: A demitasse is a small cup of strong black coffee, from French for half-cup.
